children: Oil fell as early signs suggested talks between the United States and Iran on reopening the world’s most important energy transport route were making progress. According to Sina Finance, WTI futures fell about 2.3% to settle near $92 a barrel, while Brent futures also declined.

Copper rose for a second straight week as traders watched the demand outlook. According to Sina Finance, LME copper was little changed at $14,622.5 a ton, while aluminum rose 0.6%, nickel fell 1%, zinc fell 1.4%, tin rose 0.6%, and lead fell 0.3%.

Gold was set to post a weekly decline as elevated energy prices pushed bond yields higher and reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve may need to raise rates further to curb inflation. According to Sina Finance, spot gold rose 0.2% to $4,284.81 an ounce, and spot silver gained 0.8% to $64.2957 an ounce.

title: US Market Close | Oil Falls, Copper Flat, Gold Edges Higher
